::: {#exr-taylor}
## Taylor polynomials of the exponential function

The power series of $e^x$ converges for all $x$. Its partial sums are the Taylor polynomials
$$
  T_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{x^k}{k!}.
$$

### Implementation

Implement the function `taylor_exp(x, n)`, which returns $T_n(x)$.

::: {.lm-scaffold}
```{r}
taylor_exp <- function(x, n) {
  # ...
}
```
:::

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
taylor_exp <- function(x, n) {
  term <- 1
  total <- 1
  for (k in seq_len(n)) {
    term <- term * x / k
    total <- total + term
  }
  total
}
```
:::

### Errors

Compute the errors of $T_1(1), \ldots, T_{15}(1)$. How does the error fall?

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
ns <- 1:15
errors <- abs(sapply(ns, function(n) taylor_exp(1, n)) - exp(1))
kable(data.frame(n = ns, error = format(errors, digits = 3)))
```

The error is about $1 / (n + 1)!$, the first term left out. It falls faster and faster; after about $17$ terms, it reaches the level of the rounding errors.
:::
:::
